heuristic.applicability: Prefer when target_pose is reliable and the drawer/fixture pose is displaced relative to training, especially from the normal closed, stable, open-gripper entry or during a still-nominal pull. The policy observes two causal frames of drawer_position, drawer_velocity, target_pose, object_pose, qpos, qvel and tcp_pose; open_stop_m=0.300 m is a typed high-level argument used to form progress. Current joints and world anchor pose remain in the condition to retain reachability and robot-configuration dependence. The policy still owns every action 0:440 in all 12 occurrences, including the 300:440 overlap.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer closed or on a demonstrated opening trajectory, target_pose observable, low enough drawer velocity for the intended phase, and a reachable arm state; normal entry is open fingers and high TCP near the drawer approach.
handoff.exit_conditions: Drawer near open_stop_m (0.300 m) with near-zero velocity, gripper open after release, TCP clear of the drawer and moving above/toward the tunnel, and the block unmoved.
handoff.failure_signatures: Drawer remains below the open stop, velocity is large, fingers stay closed, TCP does not clear the drawer, IK reports material residual, or the block moves. A missed handle is not an observed recovery case.
handoff.overlap_role: Retains supervised actions 300:440 for every occurrence (140 actions, 7.0 s), covering post-handle retreat, turn and initial descent shared with retrieve_tunnel_block.
handoff.successor_readiness: Switch when the drawer is open and stable, fingers are open, and the TCP has clearance; the shared tail permits a later switch over the tunnel.

heuristic.limitations: A drawer-relative tail can move the post-release departure with the drawer even when the independently placed tunnel block moves; the dual-anchor prior covers that later displacement. Large off-manifold TCP/contact errors are not made recoverable merely by a relative frame; the current-TCP residual prior is the safer alternative for small intermediate-state deviations. It assumes target_pose is a valid rigid drawer reference and the displaced contact remains reachable and collision-feasible. Demonstrations do not establish recovery from a missed handle, premature release, wrong phase, IK nonconvergence or unseen collisions.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Use the unchanged standard Diffusion Policy backbone on flattened two-frame relational features. encode_targets obtains FK poses of demonstrated arm commands and expresses each slot in that slot's observed target_pose frame as [relative position m, relative rotation 6D, native gripper], dimension 10. decode_action reconstructs a world TCP target using the fresh current target_pose, solves IK from fresh measured joints and reports convergence, errors and limits. Inputs use only causal observations and open_stop_m. Representation normalization is fitted only to valid transformed labels. No augmentation, future inference input, auxiliary head or scripted completion is used.
heuristic.rationale: The opening path is nearly identical in world coordinates in the inspected demonstrations because the drawer is fixed, so a world-pose policy can memorize that placement. The observed target_pose is rigidly attached to drawer translation: in demo12100 it changes from x=0.125 at index 0 to x=-0.04172 at 220 and about -0.175 at 260, while commanded TCP x changes from about -0.148 near the handle at 160 to -0.3222 at 220 and -0.4452 at 260, retaining a roughly fixed drawer-frame contact offset during the pull. The decision is to learn each commanded TCP pose as position plus 6D rotation in the current observed target_pose frame, followed by the demonstrated gripper scalar. Decoding composes that relative pose with the freshly observed target_pose and calls the supplied IK solver. This makes approach, handle contact, pull, release and initial clearance actions 0:340 equivariant by construction to displacement/rotation of the observed drawer frame. This is an expected generalization benefit, not evidence that displaced-drawer trials or missed-handle recovery were demonstrated.
heuristic.statement: Drawer-frame absolute Cartesian targets for fixture-displacement equivariance

assignment.subgoal: From the common home state with the drawer closed, approach the drawer handle, close the gripper on it, pull the drawer to its approximately 0.30 m open stop, release it, and lift/turn toward the tunnel approach. Contact is with the drawer handle; the tunnel block must remain undisturbed. Approximate entry: drawer_position 0, open fingers, TCP high near world (-0.384, 0, 0.442). Approximate exit: drawer_position about 0.300 and stationary, fingers open, TCP descending toward the tunnel from above while the block is still at its initial low pose.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: FK command poses are transformed into the observed drawer frame and exactly recomposed before verified Panda IK. The check compares world TCP position in metres, rotation angle in radians and gripper scalar; only 6D Gram-Schmidt projection and nonunique IK are applied.

contract.cut_relation: Preserves actions 0:440 for all twelve assigned occurrences, including the complete action-supervised 300:440 overlap with retrieve_tunnel_block. It refines the invocation contract only by making every Cartesian label drawer-frame relative; no action or phase is removed.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is [px,py,pz,r1x,r1y,r1z,r2x,r2y,r2z,g]: an absolute commanded TCP pose expressed in the freshly observed target_pose frame, with position in metres, the first two rotation-matrix columns as 6D rotation, and native gripper scalar g. At each physical slot the decoder Gram-Schmidt projects the 6D value to SO(3), composes target_pose_world * represented_pose, and solves IK from freshly measured joints. Slots represent t-1 through t+14; execution uses slots 1 through 8. The gripper sign retains the common nonnegative-open/negative-close rule.
contract.parameter_semantics: open_stop_m is the intended drawer travel/open stop in metres, bound to 0.300 m in every authorized demonstration. It normalizes causal drawer progress. target_pose is the observed world-frame rigid drawer reference, object_pose is the tunnel block, and pose quaternions are wxyz.
